title: Only a bare cairn sudorelay acquires root
intention: cairn/devices/sudo_relay daemon.py main() acquires root only when called with no arguments: --status reports the window as today, --help / -h prints the usage (the module docstring's Start/Watch/Stop lines) and exits 0, and any other argument prints 'unknown argument <arg>' plus the usage to stderr and exits 2, without calling run().
why: Measured 2026-10-11T10:24:17 by cc0: `bin/cairn sudorelay --help` printed no usage; it started the privileged daemon, which asked sudo for a password ('sudo: A terminal is required to authenticate ... sudo auth failed — exiting, no root acquired'). Akien's running daemon (pid 1336957) was unaffected. Cause: cairn/devices/sudo_relay/daemon.py main() runs run() for every argv except --status, so any unknown word acquires root. Akien 2026-10-11: 'you wrote sudo relay. maybe you should add that.'
traces_to: CP6 (root is acquired only on the one act that means it); Law 7 (an unknown argument is a loud refusal, not a silent start).
how: cairn/devices/sudo_relay/daemon.py main() only: if not argv: return run(); is_word(argv[0], '--status') -> _print_status(); is_word(argv[0], '--help') or is_word(argv[0], '-h') -> print(USAGE), return 0; else print the refusal and USAGE to stderr, return 2. USAGE is a module constant holding the Start/Watch/Stop lines (the docstring keeps them too). bin/cmd/sudorelay's header comment gains the --help line.
falsifier: cairn/devices/sudo_relay/proofs/test_only_a_bare_call_acquires_root.py under PROVES {'8902708b6212': {'1','2','3'}}, with daemon.run monkeypatched to raise AssertionError('run reached'): (1) main(['--help']) and main(['-H']) return 0 and print the usage; (2) main(['--bogus']) returns 2, names '--bogus' on stderr, and does not reach run; (3) main([]) reaches run (the patched run raises). Hollow: the old main (anything else -> run()) reds 1 and 2.

decisions.text: Unknown arguments refuse (exit 2) rather than being ignored: on a command that acquires root, a typo must never mean 'start'. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The proof is cairn/devices/sudo_relay/proofs/test_only_a_bare_call_acquires_root.py, shaped like test_sudo_relay.py beside it (a module PROVES = {'8902708b6212': {'1','2','3'}}, one function per tooth, a main() that runs them): daemon.run is monkeypatched to raise so no root is ever asked for; tooth 1 main(['--help']) and main(['-h']) return 0 and print USAGE; tooth 2 main(['--bogus']) returns 2, names '--bogus' on stderr and never reaches run; tooth 3 main([]) reaches run. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

-h and -H are one word: arguments compare through cairn.tools.system_word.is_word, which folds case (ruled 2026-09-07), so tooth 1 runs '--help', '-h' and '--HELP' and the falsifier's -H is covered by the fold. The template test_sudo_relay.py sits beside the new proof in cairn/devices/sudo_relay/proofs/: a module-level PROVES dict, test_* functions one per tooth, and a _main() that runs them and returns the exit code. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
